title: Relative cyclic restriction model and forgetting the residual action
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring on a small coherent profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $G,H$ be profinite groups and $u:\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}\to H$ a continuous homomorphism, where $\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}$ is the discrete additive group. Put $\tau=u(1)$. Use internal $R$-modules and condensed-group actions [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. For $J=H,\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}$ let $\Gamma_J^G:\mathcal A_{G\times J}(R)\to\mathcal A_G(R)$ be the submodule fixed by $J$ after every profinite base change, retaining the $G$-action. These action categories are Grothendieck abelian and these functors are right adjoint to exact trivial-$J$ inflation, with the invariant-inclusion normalization [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation, lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. Derive them in the full ordinary action categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Restriction along $1_G\times u$ gives a natural transformation of triangulated functors on $D^+$,
$$\beta^G:R\Gamma_H^G\longrightarrow R\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G D(\operatorname{Res}_{1_G\times u}),$$
whose degree-zero map is the inclusion of invariant submodules. For a bounded-below complex $N^\bullet$ of $G\times\mathbf Z$-modules, let $K^G(N^\bullet)$ be the two-column total of $N^\bullet\xrightarrow{T-1}N^\bullet$, in cyclic degrees $0,1$, where $T$ acts by $1\in\mathbf Z$, with total differential $d_K+(-1)^a d_N$ in cyclic degree $a$. This defines a triangulated functor and has an invariant-normalized natural isomorphism
$$\lambda^G:QK^G(N^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G(QN^\bullet).$$
In particular, for a module $N$ put $c_N^G=(\lambda_N^G)^{-1}\beta_N^G:R\Gamma_H^G(N[0])\to Q[N\xrightarrow{\tau-1}N]$.

Forgetting the $G$-action is exact and conservative on modules and ordinary derived categories. It identifies the underlying $R\Gamma_J^G(N)$ with $R\Gamma_{R,J}(\operatorname{Res}_J N)$ for $J=H,\mathbf Z$, and takes $\beta^G,\lambda^G,c^G$ to respectively the canonical derived restriction of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus], the rank-one isomorphism of [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution], and their composite. These identifications are natural in coefficients and preserve the canonical shifts and triangle boundaries.

For $G=1$ and $N=R$ with trivial $H$-action, let $V^q=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_R(R[\underline H^q],R)$ with the inhomogeneous differential, and let $j:QV^\bullet\to\mathscr B_R(H)$ be the canonical underived-to-derived bar augmentation. With $\eta:R\Gamma_{R,H}(R[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathscr B_R(H)$ the invariant-normalized comparison of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar], one has
$$c_R^1\eta^{-1}j=Q(\epsilon),$$
where $\epsilon:V^\bullet\to[R\xrightarrow{0}R]$ is the cochain map given by the identity in degree zero, evaluation at $u(1)$ in degree one, and zero in degrees at least two. No assertion that $\beta^G$ is an isomorphism is made.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal M_R$ for internal modules. Identify them with section-ring module sheaves by [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Apply [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation] to the group sheaves $\underline G$, $\underline J$ and $\underline G\times\underline J$, for $J=H,\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}$. They are sheaves: continuous maps glue along finite profinite quotient covers (for the discrete target their finite-image clopen fibers glue). The action sites are small in the fixed coefficient universe. The presentation and [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] make all the action categories Grothendieck abelian. In particular [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] applies, including to $G\times\mathbf Z$, which is not profinite.

proof.text: For projection inflation $L_J^G:\mathcal A_G(R)\to\mathcal A_{G\times J}(R)$, the underlying module and map do not change, so it is exact by the kernel/cokernel assertion of [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation]. The sections fixed by $J$ after every base change form a submodule sheaf, stable under $G$ because the two actions commute. A map $L_J^G M\to N$ is equivariant exactly when its image lies in that submodule; restriction of its codomain and composition with its inclusion are inverse transposes. This proves $L_J^G\dashv\Gamma_J^G$ with the required normalization, also for discrete $J$. For profinite $J$ this is precisely the datum of [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation].

proof.text: Let $U_J:\mathcal A_{G\times J}(R)\to\mathcal A_J(R)$ forget $G$, and $U_0:\mathcal A_G(R)\to\mathcal M_R$. They create kernels and cokernels by the action-site presentation, and reflect zero objects and isomorphisms: the inverse of an equivariant isomorphism is equivariant. They are exact, so descend to triangulated functors on the ordinary derived categories. Exactness gives $H^n(UK)=U H^n(K)$. Thus $UK=0$ implies all $H^n(K)=0$ and $K\to0$ is a quasi-isomorphism, so $K=0$. Applying this to the cone triangle of a morphism shows that derived $U$ is conservative as well. This argument has no boundedness restriction.

proof.text: There is an exact left adjoint to $U_J$, namely $F_G(M)=R[\underline G]\otimes_R M$, with $G$ translating the free generators and $J$ acting on $M$. Indeed $[g]\otimes m\mapsto g f(m)$ and evaluation at $[1]\otimes m$ are inverse adjunction formulas, valid after every profinite base change. Here $R[\underline G]=j_{G!}R_G$: both are the sheafification of the free module on maps into the profinite test object $G$. It is flat by [lem-pc-sites-modules-j-shriek-flat], so $F_G$ is exact. The same construction with $J=1$ gives an exact left adjoint to $U_0$. Therefore both $U_J$ and $U_0$ preserve injectives by [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives]. This does not use induction along a non-profinite subgroup.

proof.text:
Use bounded-below termwise injective resolutions on the small action sites [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution], and the normalized derived functors and units $\alpha_J^G$ of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. The exact adjunctions of step 2 induce canonical derived adjunctions [lem-trf-bounded-below-derived-adjunction]. Put $V=\operatorname{Res}_{1_G\times u}$. Restriction is exact and $V L_H^G=L_{\mathbf Z}^G$. Take the derived mate of this identity square. This defines $\beta^G$. Its model equation, by [lem-trf-bounded-below-derived-mate-model], is
$$\beta^G_{QP}\alpha^G_{H,P}=\alpha^G_{\mathbf Z,VP}\,Q(\iota_P),$$
where $\iota_P:\Gamma_H^G P\to\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G VP$ is the invariant inclusion, termwise. In particular its degree-zero map is the claimed inclusion. The canonical derived adjunctions commute with canonical shifts [lem-sp-canonical-right-derived-adjunction-shift]; the mate, expressed as unit, identity and counit, consequently commutes with shifts and image-triangle boundaries.

proof.text:
For every bounded-below injective complex $I$ in $\mathcal A_{G\times J}(R)$, step 4 makes $U_J I$ a bounded-below injective complex. The equality $U_0\Gamma_J^G I=\Gamma_{R,J}U_J I$ is equality of fixed-section submodules, with identical inclusion maps. The derived resolution comparisons [lem-sp-derived-injective-resolution-naturality] therefore give a natural isomorphism
$$D(U_0)R\Gamma_J^G\cong R\Gamma_{R,J}D(U_J).$$
For $\beta$, apply its model equation in step 5 to $I$. Under these identifications it is the invariant-inclusion model equation for the canonical scalar restriction of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]; uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] identifies the transformations. This establishes equality of the actual derived arrows, not just of their degree-zero cohomology.

proof.text:
The two-column total is explicitly
$$K^G(N)^n=N^n\oplus N^{n-1},\qquad d(x,y)=(d_Nx,(T-1)x-d_Ny).$$
The actions commute, hence $T-1$ and this differential are $G$-equivariant. Squaring $d$ gives zero because $d_NT=Td_N$. A chain map acts on both summands; a chain homotopy $h$ gives the total homotopy $(h,-h)$, since the horizontal cross terms cancel. Each column functor is the underlying-module functor and is exact. Consequently a quasi-isomorphism of bounded-below inputs gives a columnwise quasi-isomorphism and hence a total quasi-isomorphism by [lem-sc-first-quadrant-total-column-comparison]. To apply the first-quadrant statement, shift the common vertical lower bound to zero and multiply column $a$ by the resulting constant sign $(-1)^{a b}$. Thus $QK^G$ descends to $D^+$.

proof.text: The shift comparison $K^G(N[s])\to K^G(N)[s]$ is $(x,y)\mapsto(x,(-1)^s y)$. For a chain map $f:A\to B$, reorder the summands of $K^G C(f)$ to those of $C(K^G f)$ and multiply each source-cone summand in cyclic degree $a$ by $(-1)^a$. Direct substitution in $d(x,y)$ gives a chain isomorphism. It is the identity on the target inclusion and agrees on the negative cone projection with the displayed shift comparison. Thus it identifies all three arrows of the cone triangles, in the convention $C(f)\xrightarrow{-p}A[1]$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Since distinguished triangles are images of cone triangles up to isomorphism, this makes $QK^G$ triangulated.

proof.text:
If $I$ is injective in $\mathcal A_{G\times\mathbf Z}(R)$, then $U_{\mathbf Z}I$ is injective by step 4. Apply [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution] with $r=1$ to $U_{\mathbf Z}I$. Its invariant normalization says that the composite
$$(U_{\mathbf Z}I)^{\mathbf Z}[0]\longrightarrow[U_{\mathbf Z}I\xrightarrow{T-1}U_{\mathbf Z}I]\xrightarrow{\lambda_R}R\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}(U_{\mathbf Z}I)$$
is the canonical derived-unit map. That last map is invertible on injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. Hence the first arrow is a quasi-isomorphism. It is the forgotten form of $\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G I[0]\to K^G(I)$, which is therefore a quasi-isomorphism by step 3. Only the stated existence and invariant-normalization clause of the scalar lattice node is used here.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: relative cyclic calculation below the tame-boundary input; agent expansion, not a claim that the blueprint states this auxiliary result.

proof.text:
For a bounded-below injective complex $I$, apply step 9 in every vertical degree. The row augmentations assemble to
$$b_I:\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G I\longrightarrow K^G(I).$$
It is a quasi-isomorphism by total comparison [lem-sc-first-quadrant-total-column-comparison]. For the row version interchange indices and conjugate the total differential by $(-1)^{a b}$; this is $1$ on each augmentation axis. A lower vertical bound is removed as in step 7. The inclusion in cyclic degree zero defines a natural map $Q\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G\to QK^G$ on bounded-below complexes. By the universal property in [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] it uniquely induces
$$\theta^G:R\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G\longrightarrow QK^G,\qquad \theta^G_{QP}\alpha^G_{\mathbf Z,P}=Q(b_P).$$
On $I$, both $\alpha_I$ and $Q(b_I)$ are invertible, so $\theta_I$ is invertible. Every derived object has such a resolution; naturality proves $\theta^G$ is an isomorphism everywhere. Define $\lambda^G=(\theta^G)^{-1}$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: relative cyclic calculation below the tame-boundary input; agent expansion, not a claim that the blueprint states this auxiliary result.

proof.text:
Here is the full normalization, which also controls naturality: for any resolution $a:N\to I$,
$$\lambda^G_N=\alpha^G_{\mathbf Z,I}\,Q(b_I)^{-1}\,Q(K^G a),$$
followed by the inverse of $R\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G(Qa)$ on its target. The equation defining $\theta$ makes this independent of all choices by the derived-unit universal property. For a cone diagram, use the cone of a map of specified injective resolutions: it is again bounded below and termwise injective, and its augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism by [lem-sp-derived-injective-resolution-naturality]. The row inclusions $b$ commute with the cone and shift identifications of step 8. On these injective models the derived units are the normalized comparisons and their shifts are canonical [lem-sp-canonical-right-derived-adjunction-shift]. The displayed formula therefore makes $\lambda^G$ a shift-compatible natural isomorphism of triangulated functors, retaining the negative cone boundary convention. On a module its map from invariants is exactly the invariant inclusion. Set $c_N^G=(\lambda_N^G)^{-1}\beta_N^G$.

proof.text: Forgetting $G$ leaves $K$, $b$ and every differential unchanged and takes a chosen injective resolution to an injective resolution. Thus the formula of step 11 becomes the scalar rank-one comparison, and step 6 takes $c^G$ to its scalar composite with restriction. More precisely, the rank-one existence theorem [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution] may and here does use the witness obtained by this same row-augmentation construction with $G=1$; it satisfies its stated naturality and normalization. We do not infer uniqueness of a derived isomorphism from its degree-zero map alone. The strengthened equation $\theta\alpha=Qb$ fixes the comparison on all bounded-below complexes. All forgetting comparisons commute with shifts and boundaries because they identify the actual resolution and cone diagrams.

proof.text:
Let $\varphi:R\to R'$ and $f:N\to s_{G\times J}N'$ be an equivariant coefficient map. The action topoi of [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction] apply to the group-sheaf projection $G\times J\to G$: its module pullback is $L_J^G$ and its direct image is $\Gamma_J^G$. On these topoi scalar restriction is direct image along the identity geometric morphism with ring map $\varphi$. The commuting scalar/projection square gives, by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] and its adjunction normalization [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], a canonical isomorphism
$$d_J:R\Gamma_J^{G,R}s_{G\times J}\xrightarrow{\sim}s_G R\Gamma_J^{G,R'}.$$
Define the coefficient map as $d_J R\Gamma_J^{G,R}(f)$. This uses derived scalar-extension adjunctions, not exactness of ordinary scalar extension. For restriction along $1_G\times u$, both paths around the coefficient square transpose to the same map $V L_H^G R\Gamma_H^G N\xrightarrow{V\varepsilon_H}VN\xrightarrow{Vf}VsN'$. Mate pasting [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] proves equality. The same pasting with forgetting gives the coefficient compatibility of step 6.

proof.text: For the cyclic coefficient square, let $N'\to I'$ be a bounded-below injective resolution over $R'$. Every augmented cyclic row for $I'$ is a quasi-isomorphism by step 9; scalar restriction is exact and leaves that row and $T-1$ unchanged, so the same is true for $sI'$, without claiming its terms are injective over $R$. Therefore $Q(b_{sI'})$ is invertible by step 10's row-total argument. The identity $K_R(sI')=s_GK_{R'}(I')$ identifies these row maps. By adjunction normalization in step 13, $d_{\mathbf Z}^{-1}$ is the derived mate of the identity $L_{\mathbf Z}^{G,R}s_G=s_{G\times\mathbf Z}L_{\mathbf Z}^{G,R'}$. Apply [lem-trf-bounded-below-derived-mate-model], whose two horizontal functors here are exact scalar restrictions. Its model equation gives $d_{\mathbf Z}\alpha_R(sI')=s_G\alpha_{R'}(I')$. Since $\theta_R\alpha_R(sI')=Q(b_{sI'})$ is invertible, $\alpha_R(sI')$ is invertible as well. Thus the defining equations $\theta\alpha=Qb$ on this common acyclic model give $s_G\lambda_{R'}=d_{\mathbf Z}\lambda_R$ under the termwise coefficient identification. Compose with $f$ and naturality to obtain the general coefficient square. Scalar comparisons commute with canonical shifts by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift]; hence the squares for $\beta,\lambda,c$ also preserve triangle boundaries.

proof.text:
It remains to prove the bar identity, now with $G=1$ and $N=R$ having trivial $H$-action. Choose a nonnegative equivariant injective resolution $a:R[0]\to I$. Use the explicit compatible bar model in [lem-sfb-internal-bar-roof-adjunction], which spells out the normalization of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar]:
$$D^{p,q}=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_R(R[\underline H^p],UI^q),\quad d_{\mathrm{Tot}}=d_h+(-1)^p d_I.$$
Its invariant-inclusion map $b_H:\Gamma_H I\to\operatorname{Tot}D$ represents $\eta$; the map $V^\bullet\to\operatorname{Tot}D$ induced by $a$ in resolution degree zero represents $j$. These are exactly statements of the cited model node, not an assumption that $V$ computes derived invariants. All diagonals here are finite because both indices are nonnegative.

proof.text:
Define $E:\operatorname{Tot}D\to K^1(VI)$, where $V$ now denotes restriction along $u$, by the identity on $D^{0,q}=UI^q$, evaluation at $\tau$ from $D^{1,q}$ to cyclic degree $1$ and vertical degree $q$, and zero for $p\geq2$. Evaluation is an internal module morphism: it is precomposition with $R\to R[\underline H]$, $1\mapsto[\tau]$, and so is natural after every profinite base change. The only horizontal chain equation needing a check is
$$(d_h m)(\tau)=\tau m-m=(T-1)m.$$
There is no target in cyclic degree two. Vertical differentials commute with evaluation and both totals use $(-1)^p$ in column $p=0,1$, so $E$ is a cochain map. Moreover $Eb_H$ is the invariant inclusion $\Gamma_H I\to K^1(VI)$, in cyclic degree zero. This calculation uses the action-dependent bar differential even though the original coefficient module $R$ was trivial: the resolution terms need not have trivial action.

proof.text:
Put $k=K^1(Va):[R\xrightarrow0R]\to K^1(VI)$; it is a quasi-isomorphism by step 7 and exactness of restriction. Steps 5 and 10 give, on the resolution $I$,
$$c_R^1=Q(k)^{-1}Q(Eb_H).$$
Indeed the derived-mate equation for $\beta$ followed by $\theta\alpha=Qb$ gives precisely the invariant inclusion into $K^1(VI)$; no injectivity of $VI$ is needed. With $\eta=Q(b_H)$ in the chosen model, cancellation yields $c_R^1\eta^{-1}j=Q(k)^{-1}Q(E)j$. On complexes, $E$ applied to the representative of $j$ is $k\epsilon$: in degree zero it is $a$, in degree one it is $a$ after evaluation at $\tau$, and in all higher degrees it is zero. Hence the last expression is $Q(\epsilon)$. The map $\epsilon$ is a cochain map since $R$ has trivial action and $d_h^0=0$. No invertibility of $\beta$ was used or obtained.
